chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام said: “Bequesting one-fifth is recommended, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has been pleased for Himself with one-fifth.”
And he said: “One-fifth is moderation, one-fourth is exertion, and one-third is unfairness.”

key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: one-fifth; here, the recommended portion for a bequest
key_terms.حَيْفٌ: unfairness or excess leading to injustice

ai.seo_question: What amount is recommended for a bequest in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith recommends making a bequest of one-fifth, presenting it as a balanced and moderate amount. It contrasts this with one-fourth as burdensome and one-third as excessive, framing the ruling in terms of measured financial responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5421 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said that the Commander of the Faithful (as) said:
"Bequeathing one-fifth (khums) is recommended because Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has chosen one-fifth for Himself."
Imam (as) also said: "One-fifth is moderation, one-fourth is exertion, and one-third is injustice."
